title: IDS: say what the file must contain, then check it

host.note: Reconstructed session: the replies were written by an agent playing this session; every embed was computed by the host from the graphs named.

request.text: Write an IDS that requires every analysed element to have Pset_NRCOperationalCarbon.OperationalCarbon_kgCO2e_per_year as a number.

reply.text: The node catalog has no node that evaluates an IDS file: of 130 node kinds, the Compliance pack only has check.required, check.rule, check.rollup, and check.union, none named check.ids or ids.*. I wrote the specification anyway, as a real IDS 1.0 file, samples/notebooks/graphs/s09-ids-check/nrc-analytics.v1.ids: one specification, IDS-OC, applying to the fourteen IFC classes that carry a row in nrc_analytics_long.csv (IFCWALL, IFCWALLSTANDARDCASE, IFCWINDOW, IFCDOOR, IFCROOF, IFCSLAB, IFCBEAM, IFCCOVERING, IFCRAILING, IFCSTAIR, IFCSTAIRFLIGHT, IFCFOOTING, IFCFURNISHINGELEMENT, IFCMEMBER), requiring Pset_NRCOperationalCarbon.OperationalCarbon_kgCO2e_per_year as an IFCREAL. I have not run it through the IDS 1.0 XSD or ids-lib, so I can't say yet that it validates against the schema. To check a model, I'll express the same requirement with check.required over the enriched model's own property sets, since no node reads the IDS file itself.

request.text: Check the enriched model against it.

reply.text: 218 elements, all Pass. The graph reads duplex-enriched's own EntityText and ParameterText, keeps the fourteen analysed classes, joins each to its Pset_NRCOperationalCarbon.OperationalCarbon_kgCO2e_per_year value (null when absent), and runs check.required on that column: 218 Pass, 0 Fail, 0 InfoNotAvailable. Every analysed element in the write-back carries the property, so this specification passes outright.

reply.text: Updated the same file with a second specification, IDS-EC, requiring Pset_NRCEmbodiedCarbon.EmbodiedCarbon_A1A3_kgCO2e on the same fourteen classes (3,099 bytes now, two specifications). Checking both against duplex-enriched: IDS-OC still 218 Pass, 0 Fail; IDS-EC is 217 Pass, 1 Fail out of 218. The one failure is the roof, "Basic Roof:Live Roof over Wood Joist Flat Roof:184483" (GlobalId 0jf0rYHfX3RAB3bSIRjmxl): it has no Pset_NRCEmbodiedCarbon at all, so the column is null for that row and check.required marks it Fail rather than passing or guessing a value.

rows: Basic Roof:Live Roof over Wood Joist Flat Roof:184483

reply.text: Yes, by the specification as written. The roof genuinely has no embodied-carbon value in this synthetic dataset (samples/nrc-analyses/nrc-q7-absence names the same element); nothing in the toolkit is allowed to infer one, so the requirement fails it honestly instead of passing on a guess. If the roof should be exempt from IDS-EC, that has to be written into the file: narrow IDS-EC's applicability to exclude IFCROOF, or add an attribute facet that carves out this element. I haven't made that change; the file on disk still requires embodied carbon on every one of the fourteen classes, roof included.

duplex-base fails both specifications outright: 0 Pass, 218 Fail on IDS-OC and 0 Pass, 218 Fail on IDS-EC, because the unenriched file carries no Pset_NRC* property sets at all, so every analysed element's value is null. duplex-enriched keeps its 218/0 on IDS-OC and 217/1 on IDS-EC. The comparison is what the write-back is for: the same check, run over the file before and after nrc-enrich-run.
